findings.location: §4, eq. (15) and the sentence after it
findings.objection: (15) claims S(a)=η(a)W_f(a+u) for a∈s⊥ and ANY u with u·s=1. It also evaluates R and S, which are functions on F_2^8, at points a∈s⊥⊂F_2^9 without naming the map between them. In PROOF.md §6 notation (V=ker v, basis map B, b=Bᵀa), the correct statement is R(b)=η(b)W_f(a) and S(b)=η(b)W_f(a+v), with η(b)=ε_g(−1)^{b·s_g}. Here u must be v, the only nonzero vector with Bᵀu=0. Why the stated form fails: take u=v+w with w∈s⊥ and Bᵀw=b0≠0. Then W_f(a+u)=±S(b+b0), so (15) would force |S(b)|=|S(b+b0)| for every b, which is false for generic f. No downstream effect: the proofs only use the s⊥ identity for R and the multiset of magnitudes off s⊥, and that multiset does not depend on u.
findings.required_fix: Replace (15) with R(Bᵀa)=η W_f(a) and S(Bᵀa)=η W_f(a+v) for a∈s⊥, with η(b)=ε_g(−1)^{b·s_g}. Cite s_g=s_h and ε_h=−ε_g from PROOF.md §6.

findings.location: §2, the sentence after (12) ('These assertions persist under a change of coordinates')
findings.objection: (11)–(12) are computed only for B in symplectic normal form and then carried over to general B in one sentence. That step needs C(MᵀBM)=M⁻¹C(B)M⁻ᵀ, which the text never proves. It is true. C(B) is the Pfaffian adjugate B♯ reduced mod 2 (B·B♯=Pf(B)·I). Over Z, det(M)·(MᵀBM)♯ = adj(M)·B♯·adj(M)ᵀ is a polynomial identity: check it on invertible B using B♯=Pf(B)B⁻¹ and Pf(MᵀBM)=det(M)Pf(B). Mod 2, det M=1, which gives the law. A second valid route: (5), |p|≤3 and 'D quadratic' are all preserved under a=Ma', because the transform of p∘M is p̂∘M⁻ᵀ. So (2) can be applied directly in normal-form coordinates. I checked rank C(B)=0/2/8, im C(B)=rad B in rank 6, and C(B)=B⁻¹ in rank 8 in normal form, and on the genuine rank-6 and rank-8 controls listed below.
findings.required_fix: Add either the Pfaffian-adjugate argument or the invariance-of-hypotheses argument.

findings.location: Suggested audits item 1, and the last paragraph of 'Suggested audits'
findings.objection: 'Enumerate e∈{−1,0,1}^256' cannot be done (3^256 cases). The '300 deterministic exact controls' are not included, specified or hashed in the snapshot, so they cannot be checked. Even if reproduced, they would test identities in a relaxed setting and say nothing about existence under the cap.
findings.required_fix: Replace the enumeration with an explicit, reproducible sampler, such as the genuine-pair generator in audit_suggestions. Archive the code and seeds, and label the runs as relaxed-class identity tests.

findings.location: Statements 1 and 3; the sentence 'Equations (1), (2), and (4) ... add location and residue information'
findings.objection: The proofs of (1), (2) and the zero-count bullets use only K̂_g, K̂_h ∈ {±256} and |K_g−K_h| ≤ 24. The proof of (4) uses no magnitude bound at all. So these identities hold for genuine odd Boolean pairs far outside the cap. They follow from the inverse-transform conditions already in the exact formulation (parent-proof §4–5). Explicit control, which deliberately violates the cap: let g' be the indicator of {0, e1+e2, e3+e4, e1+e2+e3+e4, e5+e6, e7+e8, e5+e6+e7+e8}. It has weight 7 and support XOR 0, so it is already canonical. Let h'=g'⊕1_F with F={0, e1,…,e8, all-ones}; h' has weight 15 and is canonical too. Then R(a)=2Σ_{x∈F}(−1)^{g'(x)+a·x}, so p(a)=(7−2w+(−1)^w)/4 with w=wt(a). This gives D=σ1+σ2 (polar matrix I+J, rank 8, weight 120) and Z={w∈{3,4}} with 126 points, and Σ_Z aaᵀ=I+J=B⁻¹. Also E=1+σ1+σ2+σ3+σ4, whose quartic coefficients are all 1, matching Pf(B_I). Every prediction holds, yet G'(0)=242. So (1), (2) and (4) are not obstructions on their own. They are new only relative to SHARPER's scalar relaxation; their force in Statement 2 comes from combining them with the cap-dependent slack identity.
findings.required_fix: State that Statement 1 holds whenever |K_g−K_h| ≤ 24, that Statement 3 holds for every pair of odd-weight functions, and that neither is a standalone obstruction.

review.strongest_supported_statement: Let g,h be odd-weight functions on F_2^8 with |G|+|H|≤28, canonical spectra K_g,K_h, R=K_g−K_h, p=R/8, D=p mod 2=J_g+J_h, and B the polar matrix of D. (a) p∈{−3,…,3}, p̂∈{0,±64}, and the transform of p² is divisible by 32 everywhere. (b) Z=p⁻¹(0) has even size and XOR 0, and Σ_{a∈Z} aaᵀ=C(B) over F_2. Here C(B)_ij is the Pfaffian of B with rows and columns i,j deleted (i≠j), and C(B)_ii=0; this is the mod-2 Pfaffian adjugate. C(B) has rank 0, 2, 8 when rank B ≤4, =6, =8; im C(B)=rad B in rank 6, and C(B)=B⁻¹ in rank 8. (c) If rank B≤4 and Z is nonempty, then z≥8, z≠10, and z=8 makes Z an affine 3-flat. If rank B=6, then z≥4 and z≠6, and z≥8 when wt(D)=128. If rank B=8, then z≥10, and z=10 forces wt(D)=120, so wt(D)=136 needs z≥12. (d) E=(p−D)/2 mod 2 has degree at most 4 with quartic coefficients Pf(B_I), so for fixed D it lies in a 93-dimensional affine space. (a)–(c) need only |K_g−K_h|≤24; (d) needs no bound. (e) For a balanced f on F_2^9 with Walsh peak ≤28 and support XOR s≠0, Z is exactly the Walsh-zero set of f (there are no zeros off s⊥), which gives the eight-row table of lower bounds. If Q=W_f/8 mod 2 on s⊥ has type (4,128), then f has exactly 8 Walsh zeros, forming a linear 3-dimensional subspace of s⊥ inside Q⁻¹(0). On s⊥, |W_f|=16 on the other 120 points of Q⁻¹(0) and |W_f|=24 on all 128 points with Q=1. The full magnitude histogram is one of I, II or III. All of these are necessary conditions only.
unproved_claims: The '300 deterministic exact controls, all passed' claim: nothing in the snapshot lets anyone reproduce it, and it is not used by any proof.
That (1), (2) and (4) add information to an exact formulation. They follow from the inverse-transform conditions. The 'beyond SHARPER.md' claim is shown only for (1), by the fake.
That any of Histograms I–III, or any zero-set/E pattern, is realizable by Boolean halves. This is open, and the candidate correctly does not claim it.
Exclusion of any of the eight residue types, or settling balanced NL242 existence. Not proved, and the candidate correctly does not claim either.
audit_suggestions: Genuine-pair generator for testing (1), (2), (4) and the zero-count bullets. Take a canonical odd g' (weight ≡3 mod 4, support XOR 0). Set h'=g'⊕1_F, where XOR(F)=0, Σ_F(−1)^{g'}≡0 mod 4, and max_a|Σ_{x∈F}(−1)^{g'(x)+a·x}|≤12. Then p=(1/4)Σ_{x∈F}(−1)^{g'(x)+a·x}. Test (4) on arbitrary random odd pairs, since it needs no bound. Two hand-checked controls: the rank-8 example in finding 4, and a rank-6 one. For the rank-6 control, let g'' be the indicator of {e7+e8, e1+e7, e1+e8} and F={0, e1,…,e6, e1+…+e6}. With w6 the weight of a on coordinates 1–6, this gives p=(7−2·w6+(−1)^{w6})/4, z=140, Σ_Z aaᵀ=E78+E87 (image = rad B), and E=1+σ1+σ2+σ3+σ4 on coordinates 1–6.

Brute-force the finite-set lemmas in F_2^5 or F_2^6: the rank bound (13), zero moment ⇒ size not 2, 4, 6 or 10, size 8 ⇒ 3-flat, and the six-point rank. Independent cross-check: a set with zero moments through degree 2 is the support of a codeword of RM(5,8)=RM(2,8)⊥. That code has minimum weight 8, attained by 3-flats, and no codeword of weight 10.
Test C(MᵀBM)=M⁻¹C(B)M⁻ᵀ on random M∈GL_8(F_2) and random alternating B, and check rank C(B) for each rank class.

Script the (4,128) arithmetic: the 28 canonical pairs, the two pointwise identities, the triple list from (17)–(19) with z≤16, the 48n and mod-3 exclusions, and N12+3N28=432+3a. All of these check by hand.

Possible strengthening (my own derivation, not computer-checked). In the balanced (4,128) case, E restricted to Q⁻¹(0) equals 1+1_Z, because p∈{0,±2} there. Use linear coordinates with Q=x1x2+x3x4+x5. Then (4) gives E=x1x2x3x4+A+x5·P' with deg A≤3 and deg P'≤2. Restrict to Q=0, i.e. substitute x5=x1x2+x3x4. Comparing degree-4 ANF terms forces every Plücker coordinate p_T(Z) to vanish when T meets both {1,2} and {3,4}. Because the projection of Z onto coordinates 1–4 is isotropic, this is equivalent to dim(Z∩rad B)≥2. For example, Z=span(e1,e3,e6) lies in Q⁻¹(0) and is allowed by Statement 2, but this condition excludes it: the monomial x2x4x7x8 in 1_Z cannot be matched.

For an exact (4,128) search: enumerate the orbits of admissible Z under the stabilizer of Q, impose |W_f|=24 on Q=1 and |W_f|=16 on Q⁻¹(0)\Z, branch on the three histograms, and require certificates that can be replayed independently, not bare solver verdicts.
Re-check the fake by script. By hand I confirmed the cell sizes 48/64/64/80 (via sign sums), ranks 6, all twelve-row totals, the correlations, the zero indices, and their XOR of 244.
significance_limits: Everything proved is a necessary condition. No residue type is excluded, balanced NL242 existence is unresolved, and no function is known to satisfy the full hypotheses.
Statements 1 and 3 do not depend on the cap and hold automatically for genuine Boolean pairs. They are useful for pruning searches over integer spectra, not as obstructions.
Statement 2 restricts only one of the eight types. It fixes the magnitudes on s⊥ but leaves three histograms off s⊥, every sign pattern, much of the possible location of Z, and E undetermined.
The fake shows that the scalar constraints are not enough. It does not show the new constraints are strong, and it is not a balanced-type fake, since 0 is not in its zero set.

This is a model review, not peer review or formal verification. It makes no novelty or priority judgment, and it relies on the earlier model-reviewed tools in PROOF.md, SHARPER.md and parent-proof.md.
